patch.value: Repair an incomplete release triple, instead of only reporting it every day

The release-completeness audit now runs unconditionally after Create GitHub release, so an incomplete predecessor is reported every day until it is repaired. Nothing repairs it. A run that publishes to npm and pushes its tag and then fails before creating the GitHub Release leaves a triple that no subsequent run completes, because the next run has no source changes and skips the release path entirely. That is exactly what happened here: v2026.08.28, v2026.08.29 and v2026.08.31 were published and tagged with no GitHub Release for fourteen days, and the three releases were created by hand on 2026-08-31, each body generated from its committed changelog section. The automation should do the same: for every release tag that has a published npm version and no GitHub Release, create the release from that version's changelog section. Held out of pull request 77 deliberately, because it is a write path into the releases API inside a job that already publishes to npm and pushes tags, and it deserves its own review rather than arriving inside a change about detection. Raised in review by Greptile as P1 and by CodeRabbit as a Major data-integrity finding.

For each release tag with a published npm version and no GitHub Release, the release job creates the missing GitHub Release from that version's committed changelog section; the step is idempotent, so a run with nothing to repair makes no API writes; a tag with no published npm version is never given a GitHub Release, since that would assert a release that was never published; the repair is covered by hermetic tests with an injected client and no network
